{{nihongo|'''Asamine Shrine'''|朝峯神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The enshrined deities are the following three {{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}<ref name="説明板">Explanation board within the shrine grounds.</ref>. The {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} (sacred object) is a mirror{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Deities)|1984}}.

'''Principal deity'''
* {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto}}

'''Associated deities'''
* {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto}} – Husband deity of Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto.
* {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi no Mikoto}} – Father deity of Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto.

In {{ill|Japanese mythology|Q814158|qid=Q814158|lt=the myths of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki}}, Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto has legends concerning childbirth and sake brewing; therefore, there are beliefs associated with safe childbirth, fertility, and sake brewing{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Deities)|1984}}.

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
[[File:Kera-fuji (Kochi).JPG|thumb|250px|right|Mt. Kera (Kera Fuji), regarded as a {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}}]]
The date of foundation is unknown. The shrine is situated on the western foothills of Mt. Kera (also called Kera Fuji), the northern peak of Mt. Hachibuse, and this Kera Fuji is worshipped as a {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}}{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Although the period is unclear, it is said that the shrine was originally established through a ritual transfer from {{ill|Sengen shrine|Q3471785|qid=Q3471785}} (which worships {{ill|Mount Fuji|Q39231|qid=Q39231}}){{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the surrounding area there are many late {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}} burial mounds, such as the Miyanotani Kofun, the Takamagahara Kofun group, and the Takatennbara Kofun group. The presence of Asamine Shrine is compared with the powerful clans who constructed these tombs{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

=== Historical overview ===
In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=official histories}}, it is recorded that in the 8th year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of “Asamine no Kami” was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), “Asamine Shrine” is listed in {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}}{{ill|Nagaoka District, Kōchi|Q1132123|qid=Q1132123}} and is included among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Among the place names appearing in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wamyō Ruijushō}}, the current site of the shrine is identified with Kera-go in Nagaoka District{{Sfn|Kera-go (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

During the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, the shrine was revered by the local Yokoyama clan, and inscriptions on ridge tags indicate that construction was carried out by the Yokoyama family{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. In the 16th year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1588|Q6757|qid=Q6757}}), the “Kera Estate Land Survey Register” records the shrine as “Asamine Daimyōjin,” noting its scale as “one shrine, dance hall and side hall, five ken by two ken, torii and horse ground,” along with extensive shrine lands{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it is recorded in the “Nanroshi” that in the 4th year of {{ill|Genbun|de|Genbun|fa|گنبون|fr|Ère Genbun|ja|元文|ko|겐분|ru|Гэмбун|simple|Genbun|sr|Генбун|sv|Genbun|tr|Genbun|zh|元文 (日本)|qid=Q1145754}} ({{ill|1739|Q7002|qid=Q7002}}), a lawsuit arose with the neighboring Saigyō-ji temple during repairs to the shrine buildings{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} ({{ill|1765|Q7665|qid=Q7665}}), the shrine was added as the eighth of the prayer shrines of the {{ill|Tosa Domain|Q1189704|qid=Q1189704|lt=lords of Tosa}}{{ill|Tosa-Yamauchi family|Q786351|qid=Q786351}}, and thereafter received their patronage{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Deities)|1984}}.

In the 5th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}.

=== Divine rank ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 8 ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), June 20: promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}) – recorded as “Asamine no Kami.”

=== Shrine grounds ===
The main sanctuary is located on higher ground about 10 meters from the worship hall, enshrined in front of a female-symbol rock cave called “Kame no Iwaya”{{Sfn|Asamine Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

Near Asamine Shrine there was formerly Saigyō-ji temple, which enshrined the spirit of {{ill|Minamoto no Mareyoshi|Q11564062|qid=Q11564062}} (younger brother of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}). The temple has since been abolished, but on its former site remains a seamless stupa said to be Kiyoyoshi’s grave<ref>[http://www.city.kochi.kochi.jp/soshiki/90/cas-city-3101800.html Saigyō-ji Site Seamless Stupa] (Kōchi City website).</ref>.

=== Festivals ===
* Summer Festival ({{ill|July 10|Q2689|qid=Q2689}})<ref>Festival details are based on the explanation board within the shrine grounds.</ref>
* Autumn Festival (third Sunday of October) – The festival rites are designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Kōchi City<ref name="朝峯神社祭礼"/>.
